name: Distal duplication 9q syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Cytogenetic Diagnostic Criteria for Distal 9q Duplication

criteria.description: Presence of duplication involving the distal segment of chromosome 9q confirmed by cytogenetic or molecular genetic testing
Global developmental delay or intellectual disability of variable severity
Characteristic craniofacial features including brachycephaly, hypertelorism, and broad nasal bridge
Presence of congenital heart defects such as ventricular septal defect or patent ductus arteriosus

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Confirmed distal 9q duplication by genetic testing plus presence of at least two major clinical features including developmental delay and craniofacial dysmorphism
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on genetic confirmation; clinical features can be variable.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal 9q chromosomal duplication confirmed by genetic testing
searchTerms: extra genetic material on chromosome 9q end

pathognomonic.symptomName: Characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism including brachycephaly and hypertelorism
searchTerms: short head shape and wide-set eyes
facial features with brachycephaly and hypertelorism
distinct craniofacial shape with flat head and spaced eyes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Global developmental delay or intellectual disability

common.symptomName: Congenital heart defects (e.g., ventricular septal defect)

occasional.symptomName: Skeletal anomalies including clinodactyly and joint hypermobility

searchTerms: weak immune system with frequent infections
repeated infections due to immune deficiency

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; possible hypothyroidism on thyroid panel
Immunological workup may reveal mild immunodeficiency
imaging: Brain MRI may show nonspecific white matter changes
Renal ultrasound may reveal structural anomalies
genetic: Array comparative genomic hybridization (aCGH) or karyotype showing duplication of distal 9q region
Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) confirming duplication

distinguishingFeatures: Duplication involves 9p arm rather than distal 9q
Distinct craniofacial features including prominent forehead and micrognathia
Duplication of 15q region with different neurodevelopmental profile
More frequent seizures and autism spectrum disorder

redFlags: Severe congenital heart defects requiring early intervention
Progressive neurological deterioration or intractable seizures
Failure to thrive with feeding difficulties and hypotonia
references: Molecular Cytogenetics of Distal 9q Duplications: Clinical and Genetic Characterization, Am J Med Genet A. 2019
Duplication 9q34 Syndrome: Clinical Features and Genetic Insights, Eur J Med Genet. 2021
